title: Watch mode: auto-detect and load new frames
description:
## Summary
Hot-reload new frames when they appear in the source directory.

## User Interface
- `--watch` / `-w` CLI flag to enable watch mode on startup
- 'Watch' checkbox in playback controls (next to Loop)
- Ctrl+W keyboard shortcut to toggle watch mode
- Status indicator when watching/scanning

## Architecture

### Loading Phase State Machine
Idle → InitialDiscovery → InitialLoading → Watching → IncrementalLoad → Watching (repeat)

### New Resources
- WatchConfig: enabled flag, poll interval, directory
- LoadingPhase: state machine for loading lifecycle

### Race Condition Mitigations
1. File stability check: Wait for file size to stabilize or file age > threshold before loading
2. Incremental only: Don't replace sequence, extend it with new frames
3. Frame number ordering: Insert new frames in sorted position by frame number

## Implementation Tasks
1. Add WatchConfig resource and --watch CLI flag
2. Add LoadingPhase state machine resource
3. Implement file stability checking in discovery
4. Add Sequence::merge_frames() for incremental insertion
5. Add SequenceAssets::extend_frames() for growing vectors
6. Add watch mode toggle in playback UI
7. Add Ctrl+W keyboard handler
8. Add periodic re-scan system with timer

title: Environment objects: source coordinate system / winding order
description:
Source coordinate system and winding order controls for BOTH environment objects and mesh sequences.

## Problem

Imported meshes may come from tools with different coordinate conventions (Y-up vs Z-up) or different winding orders (CW vs CCW). Currently:
- Sequence meshes have a global --source-coordinates CLI flag (SourceOrientation) but no per-sequence or runtime UI
- Environment objects have per-object axis flip checkboxes but no winding order or coordinate preset
- Neither has a unified way to set convention + winding at import time

## Requirements

### Environment Objects
1. Coordinate system preset dropdown: Y-up (glTF default), Z-up, Custom
2. Winding order toggle: CCW (default) / CW
3. Compose with existing axis flip controls
4. Preset auto-sets flips (e.g. Z-up preset sets Flip Z + swap Y/Z)

### Mesh Sequences
1. Expose SourceOrientation in the UI (currently CLI-only)
2. Winding order toggle per sequence
3. Runtime-switchable (not just at load time)

## Implementation

- lib/coordinates.rs: Already has SourceOrientation — extend with WindingOrder enum (CCW/CW) and CoordinatePreset
- lib/environment_objects.rs: Add winding_order + coordinate_preset fields, compose with swizzle
- app/environment_objects.rs: When CW winding, set double_sided or flip normals
- app/ sequence systems: React to SourceOrientation changes at runtime
- UI: Dropdown + toggle in both environment panel (env objects) and sequence settings
- lib/settings.rs: Persist both in seaview.toml

## Notes

- glTF spec mandates CCW winding and Y-up, but exported meshes often don't comply
- STL/OBJ files commonly use Z-up
- Coordinate preset auto-sets axis flips for convenience but user can override
- SourceOrientation already handles Y-up/Z-up for sequences at load time — extend, don't replace

title: Toast notifications for degenerate frames and loader warnings
description:
When seaview detects issues during loading or playback (degenerate/runt frames, failed loads, format mismatches), surface these as Toast warnings so users can see them without checking logs.

## Motivation

Currently loader warnings (degenerate frames, failed loads, budget limits) only appear in the debug log. Users running the app normally have no visibility into why a frame looks wrong or was skipped.

## Proposed Behavior

- **Degenerate frame detected at load time**: Toast warning listing the frame index and file name (e.g. 'Frame 548 (surface_005480.glb) has degenerate geometry — skipping')
- **Load failures**: Toast error with frame index and error reason
- **Section budget limits**: Toast info when loading is budget-limited (e.g. 'Loaded 673 of 2133 frames (memory budget)')
- **Format mismatch warnings**: Toast warning if mixed extensions are detected in a sequence

All toasts should also appear in the existing Toast history log (📋 button in status bar) so users can review them after the fact.

## Implementation Notes

- Toast system and history log already exist (see toast_overlay.rs, status_bar.rs history window)
- Just need to wire up MessageWriter<ToastEvent> in the relevant loader systems
- Keep toast volume reasonable — batch degenerate frame warnings if many are detected (e.g. '3 degenerate frames detected: 548, 1006, ...')

title: Single load section with draggable range bar
description:

- Draggable left edge: adjusts section start
- Draggable right edge: adjusts section end
- Dragging triggers load/unload of frames

## Data model
- LoadSection { start: usize, end: usize }
- Initially covers estimated max_frames centered on frame 0

## UI
- Bar spans full timeline width
- Filled region = loaded frames
- Empty/dimmed region = not loaded
- Drag handles at edges (cursor change on hover)
- Tooltip showing frame range

## Behavior
- Drag right edge right: queue frames for loading
- Drag right edge left: unload frames from end
- Same for left edge
- Respect memory budget (can't expand beyond limit)

title: Lighting v2: data model in lib/
description:
Define the pure data model for the new lighting system in lib/lighting/.

## Structs

### Light
Per-light state, owned after generation:
- id: Uuid
- name: String (auto-generated, e.g. 'Light 1', editable)
- position: Vec2 (XZ)
- height: f32
- intensity: f32 (lumens)
- range: f32
- cone_angle: f32
- color: Color
- visible: bool (per-light visibility toggle)

### LightGroup
- id: Uuid
- name: String (default: generation config description, e.g. 'Uniform Grid #1')
- visible: bool (group-level visibility toggle)
- lights: Vec<Light>

### LightGroupGenConfig
Used only at generation time, not stored per-light after creation:
- placement_algorithm: PlacementAlgorithm
- num_lights: usize
- coverage_pct: f32
- Default params (used as initial values for each generated light):
  - height, cone_angle, intensity, range, color

### LightingRig (Resource)
- groups: Vec<LightGroup>
- active_group: Option<usize> (which group's accordion is expanded in UI)

## Rules

- All structs in lib/ — no Entity, no Res<>, no Query<>
- Derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize where appropriate
- Methods: add_group, remove_group, add_light, remove_light, toggle_group_visibility, toggle_light_visibility
- Unit tests for all methods

title: Memory-aware frame loading with timeline UI
description:
## Summary
Implement memory-aware frame loading with a visual timeline showing loaded ranges. This is critical for handling large sequences that exceed available RAM/VRAM.

## Core Requirements

### 1. Global Config (~/.config/seaview/seaview.toml)
- User-level settings separate from per-directory seaview.toml
- Memory budget configuration (auto-detect or manual)
- Default settings that apply across all projects

### 2. Memory Budget System
- Auto-detect available RAM + GPU VRAM
- Calculate reasonable default memory budget (e.g., 50% of available)
- Estimate frame size from first loaded frame
- Compute max frames that fit in budget: `budget / avg_frame_size`
- Only load frames within budget, unload others

### 3. Timeline UI Overhaul
- Fix: slider should reach 100% (current UI bug)
- Playhead indicator: triangle/chevron pointing down at current position
- Loaded range bar: horizontal bar showing which frames are in memory
- Draggable ends: resize loaded range by dragging left/right edges
- Visual distinction between loaded vs unloaded regions

### 4. Load Section Model (Foundation for Multi-Range)
- Data model supports N load sections (ranges)
- Initial UI only uses first section
- Prepare for future: multiple non-contiguous loaded ranges

## Architecture Notes

### Frame Loading Strategy
- Ring buffer style: load frames around current position
- When playhead moves outside loaded range, shift the window
- Or: user manually positions the load window via timeline drag

### State
- `LoadSection { start: usize, end: usize }`
- `Vec<LoadSection>` in config (initially just one)
- `MemoryBudget { limit_bytes: u64, estimated_frame_size: u64 }`

## Checkpoints
1. Global config file support
2. Memory budget estimation and enforcement  
3. Timeline UI fixes (slider 100%, playhead indicator)
4. Single load section with draggable range
5. [FUTURE] Multiple load sections

title: Unify playback speed: single source of truth
description: The playback speed slider doesn't stick — dragging it causes the value to snap back to 1.0 on the next frame. Root cause is the fragile two-way sync in playback_controls_system (audit Issue 2). sequence_manager.playback_fps (FPS) and ui_state.playback.speed (multiplier) represent the same concept in different units, and the sync heuristic can't tell which side changed. title: Architecture: introduce Timeline struct, separate pure logic from Bevy systems
description:
## Problem

The timeline/load section domain is fragmented across multiple Bevy resources with UI state mixed into data structures:

### Current state
- `LoadSection` (Resource) — single `[start, end)` range + `dragging: Option<LoadSectionEdge>` (UI state leaked into domain struct)
- `SequenceManager` (Resource) — owns playhead (`current_frame`), playback state (`is_playing`, `speed`, `loop_enabled`), and `Option<Sequence>`
- `SequenceAssets` (Resource) — owns `total_frames`, loaded/unloaded state, frame handles, entity tracking
- `LoadSectionSettings` — TOML-serializable mirror, also single range
- Pure logic (clamp, center_on, set_start, set_end) lives on `LoadSection` methods — good, but the struct is a Bevy Resource with UI state
- Budget enforcement (`update_load_section_from_budget`) is a Bevy system, not callable standalone
- Frame window computation (`manage_frame_window`) is a monolithic Bevy system mixing spawn/despawn/visibility/memory tracking

- `Timeline` struct — owns `total_frames`, `Vec<LoadSection>`, playhead position

**Bevy system layer (thin wrappers):**
- Systems extract resources, call library functions, write results back
- UI state (`dragging`) lives in a separate UI-specific resource or component
- `LoadSectionSettings` maps to `Vec<LoadSection>` for multi-window persistence

**Architectural guideline:**
> Systems are thin wrappers. Logic lives in library functions that take plain arguments and return plain results.

- Refactor `LoadSection` to remove `dragging` UI state
- Introduce `Timeline` struct owning `Vec<LoadSection>`

title: GPU visibility/spawn/despawn strategy for multi-series playback
notes:
## Context

When the camera animation rig plays back across multiple mesh series, we need smart visibility/spawn/despawn logic to avoid:
- GPU thrashing from rapid spawn/despawn cycles at series boundaries
- PCIe bandwidth abuse from uploading/downloading mesh data every cut
- Frame hitches during transitions

## Terminology

See docs/terminology-reference.md. A **Series** is the atomic loadable unit (one sim run at one resolution). The camera rig orchestrates which series is active/visible at any given time.

## Design considerations

- Pre-spawn next series meshes before the camera cuts (keep invisible)
- Despawn previous series meshes after a grace period (not immediately)
- Double-buffer: keep at most 2 series worth of GPU entities alive
- Coordinate with memory budget - GPU memory for invisible pre-spawned meshes counts against global budget
- May want a transition window concept: N frames before a cut, start spawning; N frames after, start despawning
- Resolution variants (light for scrub, full for render) add another dimension — could pre-load light variant while full variant renders

## Dependencies

- Depends on: multi-series architecture (seaview-6pd)
- Depends on: camera animation rig (not yet filed)
- Related: memory budget system (MemoryBudget resource)
- Related: seaview-w5t (budget UI)

title: Ctrl+S save causes camera jump (regression)
description:
## Bug

Ctrl+S to save view still moves the camera backward from the user's perspective. This was previously filed as seaview-sks and closed, but the issue has regressed or was never fully fixed.

## Expected behavior
Ctrl+S saves the current view to seaview.toml without any camera movement.

## Actual behavior  
Pressing Ctrl+S causes the camera to jump/shift because the camera controller interprets the S key as backward movement, even with Ctrl held.

## Root cause
The camera controller still processes the S key for backward movement when Ctrl is held. The action system needs to suppress camera movement actions when modifier keys are pressed for shortcuts.

## Related
- seaview-sks (closed, same bug — regression or incomplete fix)
- seaview-ihx (input action system epic)

## Fix approach
In the input-to-actions system, suppress all camera movement actions (MoveForward, MoveBackward, etc.) when Ctrl or Cmd is held. Modifier+key combos should only fire their shortcut action, never the movement action.

title: Load section visibility model & budget rework
description:
## Summary

Replace the current hard-budget enforcement (sections get clamped/resized to fit memory) with a **visibility-based** model where sections can be freely sized but only **active** sections consume memory.

## Current behaviour (problems)

- `enforce_budget` runs every frame and shrinks sections to fit within memory budget
- Users can't freely resize sections — drags are constrained by budget
- Budget is enforced by mutating the user's layout, which is confusing and destructive

## New model

### LoadSection gets an `active: bool` field
- **Active** sections have their frames loaded into memory (consume budget)
- **Inactive** sections are just bookmarks — drawn greyed out, no memory cost
- Users can freely create, resize, and move ANY section regardless of budget

### Visibility stealing (budget enforcement via activation)
- **Creating a new section** → auto-activates it → deactivates the furthest-away active section(s) if needed to stay within budget
- **Clicking an inactive section** → activates it → deactivates furthest-away active section(s) if needed
- "Furthest away" = measured from the playhead (the most relevant reference point)
- Sections are never resized by the system — only their active flag changes

### UI changes
- Active sections: drawn with current colour palette
- Inactive sections: drawn greyed out / semi-transparent with a dimmed handle
- Click on inactive section body → activate (steal from furthest)
- Maybe a small eye icon or indicator for active/inactive state
- Remove budget constraints from `set_start`, `set_end`, `move_to` — free dragging
- Tooltip should show active/inactive status per section

## Implementation plan

### Phase 1: Data model
1. Add `active: bool` to `LoadSection`
2. Update `LoadSection::new` → active by default
3. Update `frames_to_load()` → only return frames from active sections
4. Update `compute_spawn_windows()` → only consider active sections
5. Update `total_loaded()` → only count active sections
6. New: `fn activate_section(&mut self, idx, max_frames)` — activates section, deactivates furthest from playhead if over budget
7. New: `fn deactivate_section(&mut self, idx)`
8. Rework `enforce_budget()` → toggle active flags instead of resizing sections

### Phase 2: UI
1. `load_section_bar.rs`: draw inactive sections greyed out
2. Click on inactive section body → call `activate_section`
3. Remove budget param from `set_start` / `set_end` — free dragging
4. Ctrl+drag to create → new section is auto-activated
5. Update cursor/tooltip for inactive sections
6. `apply_drag`: remove budget constraints, keep only neighbour collision

### Phase 3: Loader integration
1. `sync_section_loads`: only load frames from active sections, unload frames from deactivated ones
2. `update_timeline_budget`: toggle visibility instead of clamping sizes
3. Remove hard budget enforcement from drag path entirely

### Phase 4: Persistence
1. Add `active` field to `LoadSectionSettings`
2. Update `From` impls for serialization/deserialization
3. Backwards compat: missing `active` field defaults to `true`

## Distance metric

"Furthest away" for stealing: euclidean distance of section center from playhead.
`distance = |section.center() - playhead|`
Deactivate the section with the largest distance first.
notes:
## Clarification

Deactivating a section UNLOADS its frames from memory — this is the whole point. Active = loaded in memory. Inactive = not loaded, just a bookmark on the timeline.

The flow:
1. User creates/activates a section → frames get loaded (sync_section_loads enqueues them)
2. Budget exceeded → system deactivates furthest section → sync_section_loads sees those frames are no longer needed → unloads them (removes handles, despawns entities)
3. User clicks inactive section → reactivates → frames load back in, furthest active section deactivates and unloads

So the active flag directly controls the memory lifecycle. frames_to_load() only returns frames from active sections. sync_section_loads compares what's loaded vs what's needed and handles both loading and unloading.

title: Multi-vendor GPU VRAM detection and multi-GPU selection
description:
## Summary

Currently VRAM detection uses NVML (NVIDIA Management Library) which only works for NVIDIA GPUs. When NVML is unavailable, we fall back to a conservative 4 GB estimate. This is inadequate for AMD and Intel GPU users, and doesn't handle multi-GPU systems.

## Requirements

### 1. Multi-vendor VRAM detection
Support accurate VRAM detection across GPU vendors:

- **NVIDIA**: NVML via `nvml-wrapper` (already implemented)
- **AMD**: ROCm SMI (`librocm_smi64.so`) or sysfs (`/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total`)
- **Intel**: sysfs or `libze_loader.so` (Level Zero API)
- **Fallback**: Conservative 4 GB estimate (current behavior)

Detection should be automatic — try each backend in order and use the first that succeeds.

### 2. Multi-GPU support
Systems may have multiple GPUs (e.g. integrated + discrete, or multiple discrete cards):

- Enumerate all available GPUs with their VRAM
- Let the user choose which GPU to target for budget calculations
- Global config setting: `[memory] gpu_index = 0` or `gpu_name = "RTX 5060"`
- Log all detected GPUs at startup for visibility

### 3. Architecture
The existing `VramDetector` trait is the right abstraction. Add:

- `AmdBackend` — AMD VRAM detection
- `IntelBackend` — Intel VRAM detection
- `GpuEnumerator` — discovers all GPUs and their backends
- Config-driven selection: user picks GPU by index or name substring match

### 4. sysfs fallback for Linux
On Linux, `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total` often works for AMD and can supplement other backends. This is zero-dependency and should be tried before giving up.

## Notes
- NVML is now a required (non-optional) dependency — consider making vendor-specific backends optional features if compile times or portability become a concern
- The `debug_loader` binary should also enumerate GPUs when available
- wgpu `max_buffer_size` heuristic was removed as unreliable (reported 4096 TB on an 8 GB card)
notes: Punted: not worth building until we have live users on non-NVIDIA hardware requesting it. NVML + 4GB fallback is fine for now.

- Unload frames outside the section to stay within budget

description:

## Coupling Analysis

### Loader systems (loader.rs)

- extract_gltf_meshes: reads gltf_handles/gltf_id_to_frame, writes frame_handles/loaded_frames/loaded_count + reverse indices + memory estimation + coord_transform + mesh_materials
- track_asset_loading: reads asset_id_to_frame, writes loaded_frames/loaded_count + memory estimation + coord_transform + mesh_materials
- manage_frame_window: reads frame_entities/frame_handles/loaded_frames/mesh_materials/coord_transform/estimated_frame_bytes, writes frame_entities/displayed_frame

### UI systems (app/)
- environment_panel: Res<SequenceAssets> — reads total_frames, frame_entities (count), displayed_frame, window_range()
- rendering_section: reads total_frames, frame_entities, displayed_frame, window_range()
- material_system: reads nothing from SequenceAssets directly (uses SequenceMeshDisplay query)
- LoadingState mirror: reads loading, loaded_count, total_frames

### Other lib/ systems
- update_timeline_budget: reads total_frames
- mesh_info: reads nothing from SequenceAssets (uses SequenceMeshDisplay query)

## Proposed Split (3 resources)

### FrameStore (public, read by UI + loader)
- frame_handles: Vec<Option<Vec<Handle<Mesh>>>>
- frame_paths: Vec<PathBuf>
- frame_entities: Vec<Option<Vec<Entity>>>
- loaded_frames: Vec<bool>
- loaded_count: usize
- total_frames: usize
- displayed_frame: Option<usize>
- format: Option<MeshFileFormat>
- base_path: Option<PathBuf>
- estimated_frame_bytes: u64

Public query methods: get_frame(), get_frame_meshes(), is_frame_loaded(), progress(), window_range(), promote_to_gpu(), demote_from_gpu()

### LoaderConfig (semi-public, read by loader + material system)
- loading: bool
- mesh_materials: Vec<Handle<StandardMaterial>>
- coord_transform: Transform

### AssetIndex (private to loader)
- asset_id_to_frame: HashMap<AssetId<Mesh>, usize>
- gltf_handles: Vec<Option<Handle<Gltf>>>
- gltf_id_to_frame: HashMap<AssetId<Gltf>, usize>

## LoadSection Interaction

LoadSections live in Timeline (mod.rs) — pure, well-tested (90+ tests). The bridge is:
- sync_section_loads: watches Timeline.sections for changes, reconciles FrameStore
- manage_frame_window: reads Timeline.sections via compute_spawn_windows()
- frames_to_load(): pure function maps sections → frame indices

This bridge is clean. The refactor doesn't change the LoadSection contract — it just splits the SequenceAssets god resource that sync_section_loads and manage_frame_window currently fight over.

## UI Impact

- load_section_bar.rs: takes &mut Timeline directly, NEVER touches SequenceAssets — no change needed
- rendering_section.rs: reads SequenceAssets for display stats — switch to Res<FrameStore>
- LoadingState mirror: reads loading/loaded_count/total_frames — split across FrameStore + LoaderConfig

## Key Benefit

FrameStore (read-heavy, many consumers) separates from AssetIndex (write-heavy, loader-only). Bevy can schedule UI reads in parallel with loader writes to AssetIndex.

title: Input action system: decouple keystrokes from UI/camera actions
description:
Create a canonical input→action mapping layer so all input handling is centralized and all systems query action state instead of raw keys.

## Problem

Input handling is scattered across multiple systems:
- camera.rs reads WASD/mouse directly
- playback.rs reads keyboard for frame stepping, Ctrl+S
- menu_bar.rs reads Ctrl+S via egui
- Various UI systems check for hotkeys independently

This makes it hard to:
- Know if the user is 'Moving' when we want to enable scroll-speed-adjust (seaview-yzs)
- Add rebindable keys
- Avoid input conflicts (egui eating keys vs game systems)
- Reason about what the user is doing at any moment

## Architecture

### 1. Action Enum (lib/)
Pure data, no Bevy types:
```
enum Action {
    MoveForward, MoveBackward, MoveLeft, MoveRight,
    MoveUp, MoveDown,
    SpeedModifierSlow, SpeedModifierMedium, SpeedModifierFast,
    RotateCamera,
    NextFrame, PrevFrame, PlayPause,
    SaveView, ToggleUI, CenterOnMesh,
    // ...
}
```

### 2. Action State Resource (app/)
```
ActionState {
    active: HashSet<Action>,          // currently held/active
    just_pressed: HashSet<Action>,    // pressed this frame
    just_released: HashSet<Action>,   // released this frame
}
```

Derived states:
- is_moving() -> any movement action active
- is_rotating() -> RotateCamera active
- movement_direction() -> Vec3 from active movement actions

### 3. Input Mapping Resource
```
InputMap {
    key_bindings: HashMap<KeyCode, Action>,
    mouse_bindings: HashMap<MouseButton, Action>,
    modifier_bindings: ...
}
```
Default mappings, overridable via settings.

### 4. Systems

- **input_to_actions** (PreUpdate): Reads raw keyboard/mouse input + InputMap, writes ActionState. Single system, one place for all input.
- **camera_controller**: Reads ActionState instead of raw keys
- **playback controls**: Reads ActionState instead of raw keys
- **scroll speed adjust**: Queries ActionState.is_moving() to enable scroll behavior

### 5. egui Integration
- Actions consumed by egui (text fields, menus) are filtered out before reaching ActionState
- egui hotkeys (Ctrl+S in menu) fire through the same action system

## Subtasks
1. lib/actions.rs: Action enum + ActionState pure model
2. app/input.rs: InputMap resource + input_to_actions system
3. Migrate camera_controller to ActionState
4. Migrate playback keyboard handling to ActionState
5. Migrate menu hotkeys to ActionState
6. Implement seaview-yzs (scroll speed) using ActionState.is_moving()

## Notes
- This is NOT Leafwing Input Manager — keep it simple, bespoke, minimal
- lib/ side stays pure (no Bevy deps)
- Start with read-only migration (both old and new coexist), then cut over
- Keybinding persistence in seaview.toml comes later

title: Keyboard input handling: modifier keys conflict with camera movement
description:
## Bug

Keyboard input handling is generally wonky — modifier-key shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+PageDown, etc.) also trigger camera movement actions because the base key (S, W, PageDown) is processed independently of the modifier.

## Symptoms
- Ctrl+S moves camera backward (S = MoveBackward)
- Ctrl+W may trigger camera forward movement
- Any Ctrl+key combo can cause unintended side effects
- The action system doesn't properly gate camera movement when modifiers are held

## Root cause
The input_to_actions system in app/input.rs processes base keys and modifier combos independently. When Ctrl is held:
1. The modifier combo (e.g. Ctrl+S → SaveView) fires correctly
2. But the base key (S → MoveBackward) ALSO fires because there's no suppression

## Fix
The input_to_actions system should:
1. When a modifier key (Ctrl, Cmd, Alt) is held, suppress all camera movement actions
2. Only process shortcut actions (SaveView, ToggleWireframe, NextSeries, etc.) when modifiers are active
3. Camera movement actions should only fire when NO modifier keys are held

## Related
- seaview-ihx (parent epic — input action system)
- seaview-60g (Ctrl+S camera jump regression)
- seaview-sks (original Ctrl+S bug, closed)

title: Zero-copy mmap-friendly mesh format for instant GPU upload
notes:
## Motivation
Loading STL/glTF files requires: read bytes → parse → build Mesh struct → upload to GPU. Each step copies data. For large simulation sequences (thousands of frames), this is a major bottleneck even with async I/O.

## Goal
Design/adopt a binary mesh format where the on-disk layout matches the GPU vertex buffer layout exactly, enabling:
- **mmap** the file directly (no read + allocate)
- **Zero-copy upload** to GPU (or near-zero — just pass the mmap'd pointer)
- Potentially use persistent mapped buffers or `wgpu::BufferDescriptor::mapped_at_creation`

## Candidate Approaches
1. **Custom .svmesh format** — flat binary: header (vertex_count, index_count, format flags) + raw vertex data (pos f32×3, normal f32×3, uv f32×2 = 32 bytes/vertex) + raw u32 indices. File IS the GPU buffer.
2. **Quantized variant** — half-float positions/normals for 2× density, with bounding box in header for dequant.
3. **Pre-bake pipeline** — CLI tool converts STL/glTF → .svmesh on first load, caches alongside originals. Subsequent loads are instant mmap.

## Key Considerations
- Vertex format must match Bevy's `Mesh` attribute layout (or we bypass Mesh and create `wgpu::Buffer` directly)
- Endianness: assume little-endian (x86/ARM), add magic number for validation
- File alignment: align vertex/index data to 4096 bytes (page boundary) for mmap efficiency
- Could use `memmap2` crate for safe mmap
- Bevy's asset system may need a custom loader that returns a pre-built Mesh from raw bytes without parsing
- Look at: usf (Universal Scene Format), meshopt's quantized formats, Omniverse MDL

## Architecture Notes
- Converter lives in `lib/asset_loaders/` (pure logic) + `bin/` CLI tool
- Custom AssetLoader for .svmesh returns Mesh with zero/minimal processing  
- Existing STL/glTF support stays — .svmesh is an optional fast path
- First-load converts and caches; subsequent loads mmap

## Related
- seaview loading pipeline analysis identified file parsing as async but still CPU-heavy
- This pairs with load throttling (separate issue) — even with throttling, faster per-frame load = better

title: Material system unification: env objects, sequence meshes, presets, groups
description:
Architectural analysis and rework of the material system across Seaview.

## Problem

Materials are currently handled in three separate, incompatible ways:

1. **Sequence meshes** — MaterialConfig resource (base_color, roughness, metallic, emissive, opacity, double_sided) applied globally via apply_material_config system
2. **Environment objects** — MaterialOverride enum (Default/Preset/Custom) with per-object override, applied via sync_materials system
3. **Network meshes** — Hardcoded blue StandardMaterial in poll_network_meshes

Each has its own UI, its own state model, its own persistence path, and its own set of defaults. There's no shared material vocabulary, no reusable presets, and no way to apply the same material to both a sequence mesh and an environment object.

## Goals

- **Unified material model** in lib/ — one Material struct that works for all mesh types
- **Material groups/categories** — Liquid (water, oil, lava), Metal (steel, copper, gold), Rock (granite, sandstone, slate), Terrain (grass, sand, snow), Glass, Plastic, etc.
- **Shared preset library** — presets usable by both env objects and sequence meshes
- **Per-mesh-type defaults** — sequence meshes default to 'Liquid/Water', env objects default to 'Default (GLB)', network meshes default to something visible
- **Unified UI** — material picker widget reusable across panels (environment panel, material section, future per-mesh overrides)
- **State consolidation** — one authoritative material store, mirrors in UI

## Subtasks (to be broken out)

1. Architectural analysis — map all current material paths, identify shared state
2. lib/materials.rs — unified Material model with category/group taxonomy
3. Preset library with TOML-loadable user presets
4. Shared material picker egui widget
5. Migrate MaterialConfig (sequence meshes) to new model
6. Migrate MaterialOverride (env objects) to new model
7. Migrate network mesh materials
8. Persistence unification in seaview.toml
9. Default material assignment per mesh type

## Notes

- This is a rework epic, not urgent. Current system works, just fragmented.
- The env object MaterialOverride was built for quick iteration — it's a good starting point for the unified model
- Consider whether material groups should be enums or data-driven (TOML catalog)
- Keep lib/ pure: no Bevy types in the material model

title: Spatial accelerator: feature-gated plugin with lazy/async BVH builds
description:
## Problem

Building parry3d BVH (QBVH) acceleration structures eagerly for every loaded frame is catastrophically expensive (~300-700ms per frame on 380K-760K tri meshes). With 970 frames loading, this freezes the UI for minutes.

## Current State

- `SpatialMesh` wraps parry3d `TriMesh` — BVH is rebuilt from scratch on every construction
- `build_spatial_meshes` system runs synchronously on main thread
- No caching: BVH is never serialized/deserialized
- Time-budgeted deferred queue added but 1 build still takes 300-700ms (budget is meaningless)

## Solution: SpatialAcceleratorPlugin

Feature-gate the entire spatial subsystem behind `spatial` feature flag:

1. **SpatialAcceleratorPlugin** — single plugin owning all spatial resources/systems
2. **Lazy on-demand builds** — only build BVH when actually needed (ray cast, point query)
3. **Async task pool** — move BVH construction off main thread
4. **BVH caching** — serialize/deserialize alongside GLB files to avoid rebuilds
5. **Current-frame priority** — playhead frame built first, background frames queued

## Sub-issues

- Feature-gate plugin (remove from loader chain, make resources optional)
- Lazy build path (`ensure_built` called from consumers)
- Async BVH construction via Bevy task pool
- BVH disk cache (sidecar files or embedded in GLB)
- Time-slider aware preloading (build BVH for nearby frames)

title: Background-thread BVH builds with disk caching and sparse sampling
description:
## Overview

When the `spatial` feature is enabled, BVH construction must not block the main thread. This issue covers the full pipeline: async building, disk caching, and sparse sampling to avoid building BVH for every frame.

## Design

### 1. Async BVH construction (off main thread)

- Use Bevy's `AsyncComputeTaskPool` to build `SpatialMesh` on worker threads
- `build_spatial_meshes` system dispatches tasks instead of building inline
- A polling system collects completed tasks and inserts into `SpatialIndex`
- Playhead frame gets priority: dispatched first, polled eagerly

### 2. Disk caching (sidecar files)

- After building a BVH, serialize parry3d's `TriMesh` (which includes the QBVH) to a sidecar file alongside the GLB, e.g. `surface_000010.bvh` or `surface_000010.glb.spatial`
- On load, check for sidecar first — if present and fresh (mtime >= GLB mtime), deserialize instead of rebuilding (~instant vs 300-700ms)
- parry3d's `TriMesh` likely supports serde — verify and use bincode/rkyv for compact fast serialization
- Cache format should include a version tag for invalidation

### 3. Sparse sampling (only cache every Nth frame)

- For a 2000-frame sequence, building+caching all BVHs is wasteful — geometry between adjacent frames is nearly identical
- Only build BVH for every Nth frame (e.g. N=10, so ~200 BVHs for 2000 frames)
- On cache miss (frame not in the sampled set): find nearest cached BVH and reuse it
  - For ray casting, the nearest-frame BVH gives approximate results that are good enough for hover/selection
  - AABB queries are even more tolerant of approximation
- Sampling rate could be configurable or adaptive (denser near keyframes/discontinuities)
- When exact results are needed (e.g. precise measurement tool), build the exact BVH on demand via `ensure_built()`

### 4. Build-on-demand triggers

- Ray cast query (hover, click) → ensure current frame's BVH exists (exact or nearest-cached)
- BVH gizmo visualization → ensure current frame
- Spatial section UI (AABB display) → ensure current frame
- Scrubbing timeline → use nearest cached, don't block

## Implementation order

1. Async task pool dispatch (biggest perf win — unblocks main thread)
2. Disk caching with sidecar files (avoids rebuilds across sessions)
3. Sparse sampling with nearest-neighbor fallback (reduces total work by ~90%)

## Perf targets

- Zero main-thread stall from BVH during loading
- BVH available for current frame within ~1 second of first display (async build)
- Cached BVH load: <5ms per frame
- Sparse sampling: ~200 BVHs for 2000-frame sequence instead of 2000

title: SpatialQuery trait: brute-force default, BVH accelerator behind trait
description:
## Insight

Spatial queries (ray cast, point projection, AABB) don't need a BVH. Brute-force over triangles is ~5-15ms for 760K-tri meshes — perfectly fine for interactive hover/click at mouse-event frequency (~60Hz input, but queries only happen on mouse move/click).

The BVH is an *optimization*, not a requirement. Extract a trait so:
- Brute-force works immediately, no feature flag needed, no caching, no async
- BVH accelerator slots in later behind the same trait when seaview-n3o.2 lands

## Design

```rust
pub trait SpatialQuery {
    fn cast_ray(&self, origin: Vec3, direction: Vec3, max_dist: f32) -> Option<RayHit>;
    fn project_point(&self, point: Vec3) -> PointProjection;
    fn aabb(&self) -> (Vec3, Vec3);
}
```

Two implementations:
1. **BruteForceMesh** — iterates all triangles. O(n). No build step, instant construction from vertex/index data. Good enough for interactive queries.
2. **AcceleratedMesh** (existing SpatialMesh) — parry3d TriMesh with QBVH. O(log n). Expensive to build (~300-700ms), but fast queries. Behind `spatial` feature.

## Benefits

- Spatial queries work out of the box without `--features spatial`
- No BVH build step means no perf hit during loading
- BVH becomes a transparent upgrade path, same API
- BruteForceMesh construction is instant (just store refs to vertex/index buffers)
- Only need to build for the *current displayed frame*, not all loaded frames

## Implementation

1. Extract `SpatialQuery` trait from existing `SpatialMesh` methods
2. Add `BruteForceMesh` implementing the trait (iterate triangles, Möller-Trumbore intersection)
3. `SpatialIndex` stores `Box<dyn SpatialQuery>` (or enum dispatch)
4. Default path: build BruteForceMesh on frame display (instant)
5. `spatial` feature: upgrade to AcceleratedMesh when available

title: Persistent UI state system: derive macro + hierarchy-aware trait
description:
Design and implement a general-purpose system for persisting UI state across sessions.

## Problem
Currently, saving UI state requires manually wiring each resource into handle_save_view, the Settings struct, and restoration code. Adding new persistent state means touching 3+ files. There's no way for a UI module to declare 'I have state that should be saved' without coupling to the central save system.

## Desired behavior
A trait + derive macro system where any UI state struct can opt into persistence:

```rust
#[derive(Resource, PersistentState)]
#[persist(key = "ui.collapsible")]
pub struct CollapsibleState {
    pub environment_light_open: bool,
    pub lighting_rig_open: bool,
    // ...
}
```

Key properties:
- **Derive macro**: `PersistentState` auto-implements the trait, registers with the hierarchy
- **Hierarchy-aware**: nested structs participate automatically (e.g. `ui.collapsible.lighting_rig_open`)
- **Automatic save/load**: a single system collects all `PersistentState` resources and serializes them — no manual wiring needed
- **Key-based addressing**: each piece of state has a dotted key path (e.g. `ui.panel.scroll_y`)
- **Serde-backed**: leverages existing Serialize/Deserialize on the structs
- **Backwards-compatible**: missing keys get defaults, extra keys are ignored

## Scope
- PersistentState trait definition
- Derive macro (or manual impl for v1)
- Collection system that gathers all PersistentState resources on save
- Restoration system that hydrates resources on startup
- Migration from current manual Settings wiring
- Integration with seaview.toml (or a separate ui_state.toml)

## Open questions
- Should this live in lib/ or app/?
- Separate file from seaview.toml? (ui_state.toml vs merged)
- How to handle resources that don't exist yet at load time (lazy registration)?
- Should the macro generate the Bevy Resource derive too?

title: Research Bevy SSR / IBL for water rendering
description:
## Problem

Current water rendering relies entirely on PBR material settings (base color, roughness, metallic, reflectance) but without screen-space reflections (SSR) or environment map reflections, the surface looks flat and unrealistic regardless of material tuning.

Water appearance in reality comes primarily from:
- Fresnel-driven reflections (sky, environment) at glancing angles
- Specular sun glint path
- Subsurface scattering / absorption for depth color

None of these are active with just StandardMaterial.

## Research needed

1. Bevy SSR — Does Bevy 0.15+ have SSR support? What is the API? Performance cost?
2. Environment maps / skybox — Can we add an HDRI skybox that the PBR pipeline reflects? This alone would massively improve water appearance.
3. EnvironmentMapLight — Bevy has EnvironmentMapLight component for image-based lighting (IBL). Investigate using this instead of / alongside directional + ambient.
4. Custom water shader — If SSR is not available, would a custom shader (normal-mapped waves, animated Fresnel, fake reflections) be worth it?
5. Bevy render graph — Check if there are community plugins (bevy_water, bevy_ssr) that could be integrated.

## Acceptance criteria

- Document what is available in our Bevy version
- Prototype at least one approach (SSR, IBL/skybox, or custom shader)
- Compare visual quality before/after with screenshots
- Estimate performance impact on target hardware

## Problem

loadfu's GlbLoader claims both .glb and .gltf extensions but reads the entire file as a byte slice and parses it as binary GLB. This fails for multi-file .gltf (e.g. Khronos Sponza) which has external references to .bin buffers and .jpg/.png textures:

    glTF error: external reference in slice only import

The error spams every frame because the loading tracker keeps retrying the failed asset.

## Root Cause

- vendor/loadfu/src/bevy_integration/asset_loaders.rs: GlbLoader::extensions() returns ["glb", "gltf"]
- glb::parse_merged(&bytes) cannot resolve external URI references from a byte slice
- The sequence loader (load_mesh_handle) loads all glTF formats as Handle<Mesh> through loadfu

## Solution: Option 1 — Bevy native for .gltf

1. loadfu: Change GlbLoader::extensions() to ["glb"] only
2. Sequence loader: Detect .gltf files and use a two-phase loading path:
   - Phase 1: asset_server.load::<Gltf>(path) -> Handle<Gltf> (Bevy native GltfLoader handles external references)
   - Phase 2: Extract Handle<Mesh> from the loaded Gltf asset (via GltfMesh primitives)
3. .glb files: Continue using loadfu fast direct-to-Mesh path (no change)

## Files to Change

- vendor/loadfu/src/bevy_integration/asset_loaders.rs — strip .gltf from extensions
- vendor/loadfu/src/bevy_integration/plugin.rs — update docs
- crates/seaview/src/lib/sequence/loader/mod.rs — add two-phase detection
- crates/seaview/src/lib/sequence/loader/load_queue.rs — branch: .glb -> Handle<Mesh>, .gltf -> Handle<Gltf> + extraction
- crates/seaview/src/lib/sequence/loader/loading_tracker.rs — handle Gltf asset events alongside Mesh events
- crates/seaview/src/lib/sequence/loader/assets.rs — may need to store Handle<Gltf> alongside Handle<Mesh>

## Test Case

Khronos Sponza: assets/models/Sponza/glTF/Sponza.gltf — multi-file .gltf with 70+ texture references and external .bin buffer.

## Also Fix

The loading tracker retries failed frames every frame indefinitely — add a max-retry limit or mark permanently failed frames to stop the error spam.

title: Per-series mesh transform: data model + settings persistence
description:
Each series needs its own transform (position, rotation, scale) so users can offset/align multiple sim runs visually. Currently there's no per-series transform anywhere.

Add:
- lib/series.rs: SeriesState gets a 'transform: Transform' field (Bevy Transform, default identity)
- lib/settings.rs: SeriesSettings gets position/rotation/scale fields, roundtrip to/from SeriesState
- seaview.toml: [[series]] entries gain position = [x,y,z], rotation = [x,y,z,w], scale = [x,y,z]
- Backward compat: missing fields default to identity transform

The transform is applied to all spawned frame entities for that series by the frame_window system (or a new sync system). When switching series, the active series' transform is applied to the mesh root.

title: EXR/HDR skybox support — load user-provided HDRI files as environment maps
notes:
## Summary

Add support for loading .exr and .hdr HDRI files as environment maps (skybox + IBL).

Currently the environment map system only supports pre-baked KTX2 cubemap pairs (diffuse + specular) with a hardcoded naming convention. Users cannot drop in their own .exr/.hdr files.

## What needs to happen

1. **Enable Bevy image features**: Add `"exr"` and `"hdr"` to the bevy features in workspace Cargo.toml
2. **Equirectangular HDR skybox**: Load a single .exr/.hdr as an equirectangular skybox image. Bevy's `Skybox` component can use a single cubemap or equirectangular image directly.
3. **Discovery**: Scan the `environment_maps/` asset dir for .exr/.hdr files alongside the existing .ktx2 convention. Register them in EnvironmentMapCatalog.
4. **UI**: The existing environment panel dropdown should show both KTX2 and HDR/EXR entries seamlessly.
5. **IBL consideration**: For full IBL (diffuse irradiance + specular pre-filtered), the equirectangular map would need to be converted to a cubemap pair at runtime. This could be a follow-up — start with skybox-only for HDR/EXR files.

## Current state

- EnvironmentMapCatalog only registers KTX2 pairs with hardcoded path convention
- Bevy features `exr` and `hdr` are not enabled
- Only 'Pisa' environment map is registered
- ExrTextureLoader exists in Bevy but is behind cfg(feature = "exr")

## Files involved

- Cargo.toml (workspace) — bevy features
- crates/seaview/src/lib/lighting/environment_map.rs — catalog, config, sync
- crates/seaview/src/lib/lighting/mod.rs — plugin setup, catalog registration
- crates/seaview/src/app/ui/systems/environment_panel/mod.rs — UI

title: Memory budget UI: per-series allocation visibility
notes:
## Context

With multi-series support (seaview-6pd), the global memory budget is shared across all loaded series. Users need visibility into how the budget is being consumed.

## Terminology

See docs/terminology-reference.md. **Series** = atomic loadable unit. Each series has its own load sections that nibble from the global memory pool.

## What users need to see

- How much of the budget each series is consuming (bytes and frame count)
- Which series have active load sections eating into the pool
- How much headroom remains for pre-loading the next series
- Per-series frame size estimates (resolution variants have very different per-frame costs)

## Design considerations

- Status bar or panel showing budget breakdown by series
- Visual indicator when pre-loading a second series is competing with the active one
- Possibly allow manual budget allocation hints (e.g. reserve 30% for pre-load)
- Should integrate with existing MemoryBudget resource
- Resolution variants make this interesting: light variant might be 10x cheaper per frame than full

## Dependencies

- Depends on: multi-series architecture (seaview-6pd)

title: Environment objects: axis swizzle controls
description:
Add per-object axis swizzle controls to the Environment Objects UI panel.

## Problem

Imported GLB landscape/terrain files may have different axis conventions, appearing flipped or rotated. Users need a quick way to remap axes without manually computing rotation angles.

## UI Design

Three rows (one per output axis), each with 6 toggle buttons:

    X:  [-x] [+x] [-y] [+y] [-z] [+z]
    Y:  [-x] [+x] [-y] [+y] [-z] [+z]
    Z:  [-x] [+x] [-y] [+y] [-z] [+z]

Default mapping: X->+x, Y->+y, Z->+z (identity).

Only one button per row is active at a time (radio-style). Selecting e.g. X->-z means the output X axis reads from the negated source Z axis.

## Implementation

- lib/environment_objects.rs: Add AxisSwizzle struct to EnvironmentObject (3 axis mappings, each with source axis + sign)
- app/environment_objects.rs: Convert swizzle to a rotation/scale matrix and compose with the existing Transform3D before applying to Bevy Transform
- app/ui/systems/environment_panel/objects_section.rs: Render the 3x6 button grid in the per-object controls
- lib/settings.rs: Persist swizzle in seaview.toml

## Notes

- This is a visual-only transform -- does not modify the underlying mesh data
- Compose swizzle BEFORE position/rotation/scale so users can fine-tune on top
- Common presets could be added later (Y-up to Z-up, etc.)

title: Camera: scroll wheel adjusts base movement speed during WASD
description:
When the user is actively moving (holding WASD), scroll wheel should adjust the base movement speed. Speed modifiers then multiply on top of that.

## Current behavior

- WASD moves at a fixed base speed
- Shift/Alt/Ctrl apply multipliers to that fixed speed

## Desired behavior

- While holding any WASD key, scroll wheel up/down increases/decreases the base movement speed
- The adjusted speed persists for the session (sticky)
- Modifier keys apply on top of the adjusted base speed:
  - Shift: base × 5
  - Alt: base × 25
  - Ctrl: base × 125
- Without any modifier: just the base speed
- Speed could be shown briefly in the HUD or status bar when changed

## Implementation

- app/systems/camera.rs: Track base_speed in FpsCamera or a Local resource
- Read scroll wheel delta when any WASD key is held
- Multiply/divide base_speed by some factor per scroll tick (e.g. 1.2× per tick)
- Clamp to reasonable min/max range
- Apply modifier multipliers on top: shift 5×, alt 25×, ctrl 125×
- Consider persisting base_speed in seaview.toml

title: loadfu: full GLB feature parity (except animations)
description:
## Goal

loadfu currently produces `Handle<Mesh>` for all formats (STL, OBJ, PLY, GLB). For GLB, this strips everything beyond geometry — materials, textures, scene hierarchy, cameras, lights are all lost. The environment objects system still falls back to Bevy's built-in `bevy_gltf` loader for GLB scene support.

**Objective:** Make loadfu produce everything GLB supports (except animations), so we can unify all env object loading through loadfu and eventually drop the dual-loader architecture.

## Current State

- `GlbLoader` → `Handle<Mesh>` (merged or per-primitive). Geometry only.
- `AssetData` already supports `Vec<MeshData>` + `Vec<MaterialData>` in core
- `AssetCapabilities` exists with pre/post-parse capability querying
- `MaterialData` has PBR fields (base_color, metallic, roughness, has_textures) but doesn't flow through to Bevy
- `into_mesh.rs` only converts geometry — no material or texture conversion
- Environment objects use two code paths: loadfu for STL/OBJ/PLY, `bevy_gltf` for GLB
- `RenderAssetUsages::MAIN_WORLD` default means direct-mesh assets need manual GPU promotion (just fixed)

## Sub-tasks

### 1. Scene-level asset output
- New `AssetLoader` impl that produces a scene-like structure (not just `Mesh`)
- Multiple meshes with per-node transforms
- Parent-child hierarchy preservation
- Could produce `Handle<Scene>` or a custom `LoadfuScene` asset

### 2. PBR materials → Bevy `StandardMaterial`
- Map `MaterialData` → `StandardMaterial` (base_color, metallic, roughness, emissive)
- Per-mesh material assignment
- Alpha mode support (opaque, mask, blend)
- Double-sided flag

### 3. Texture loading
- Base color texture (albedo)
- Normal map
- Metallic-roughness map
- Emissive map
- Texture coordinate support (UV0, UV1)
- Texture transform support (KHR_texture_transform)

### 4. Capability-driven UI
- `AssetCapabilities` already exists — wire it to UI layer
- Hide UV/material controls when format doesn't support them
- Show material properties panel only when materials are present
- Per-format info in environment panel

### 5. Unify env object pipeline
- Remove dual-loader architecture (loadfu + bevy_gltf)
- All formats go through loadfu → one code path in environment_objects.rs
- Simplify `LoadedAsset` enum — no more `Gltf` vs `DirectMesh` distinction
- Fix `RenderAssetUsages` at the loader level (not per-consumer)

## Out of scope (for now)
- Animations / skeletal meshes
- Cameras and lights from GLB scenes
- glTF extensions beyond KHR_texture_transform
- Draco / meshopt decompression (separate issue)

## Research references
- `docs/research/mesh_loading_ecosystem.md` — MeshSource trait design, capability table
- `docs/research/mesh_formats_comparison.md` — format feature matrix
- `docs/research/mesh-loading.md` — original loading architecture research
- `vendor/loadfu/src/capabilities.rs` — existing AssetCapabilities, MaterialData
- seaview-bdz.4 (closed) — MeshSource trait, superseded by loadfu but capability design still relevant
notes:
## Design Notes

### Key architecture decisions needed:
1. **Asset type**: Should loadfu produce `Handle<Scene>`, a custom `Handle<LoadfuScene>`, or stay as `Handle<Mesh>` with material handles as labeled sub-assets?
2. **Texture pipeline**: How to route texture data through Bevy's asset system (embedded images vs file references)
3. **RenderAssetUsages**: Fix at loader level (`MAIN_WORLD | RENDER_WORLD` default) or keep current MAIN_WORLD-only for sequence memory management?

### The RenderAssetUsages question
Sequence meshes intentionally use MAIN_WORLD-only for memory windowing (promote/demote). Env objects need RENDER_WORLD. Options:
a) Fix in loader (always both) — simpler but sequences lose memory control
b) Loader setting — `RenderAssetUsages` in loader settings
c) Post-load promotion (current approach) — works but fragile

Option (b) is probably best.
